at øve.explanation: "At øve" means to practice, and it is very useful for a learner: "Jeg øver mig i dansk" (I am practising Danish). Danish usually adds the little word "mig" (myself) with it: "at øve sig". It is a friendly word with a simple, predictable pattern. The word for a practice or exercise is "en øvelse".

en øl.explanation: "En øl" is a beer. The plural is the same as the single form, so "to øl" means two beers. Beer is a big part of Danish culture, and a common toast is "Skål!" when you lift your glass. You can order it with "en stor øl" (a large beer) or "en lille øl" (a small one).

sentence.en: I will have a beer, please.

et øje.explanation: "Et øje" is an eye. The word for more than one is "øjne", with an n instead of an e at the end. You will use it for colors too: "Hun har blå øjne" (She has blue eyes). The word also appears in "at lukke øjnene" (to close your eyes).

et øjeblik.explanation: "Et øjeblik" is a moment. It is used a lot to ask someone to wait: "Et øjeblik, tak" (One moment, please). It is literally "an eye look", since "øje" is eye. Another very common phrase is "et lille øjeblik" (just a moment).

et øre.explanation: "Et øre" is an ear. The word for more than one is "ører". It also means a small coin: "øre" is one hundredth of a krone. From context it is clear which one is meant, for example "Jeg har ondt i øret" is the body part.

øm.explanation: "Øm" means sore or tender, when a part of the body hurts a little when touched. It is not the same as "ondt", which is a stronger, general word for pain. Add a "t" with et-words: "et ømt knæ". The words for more and most sore are "ømmere" and "ømmest".

sentence.en: My shoulder is sore after exercise.

øst.explanation: "Øst" is the direction east. It is used with the other points of the compass: "nord", "syd", "vest", and in names like "Østjylland" (East Jutland). "Østen" with "the" can also mean the Far East. The word for eastern is "østlig", and the word for "from the east" is "fra øst".

sentence.en: The sun rises in the east.
